output.brief: The August drop is almost entirely explained by the CH-2 chiller failure, which hit floors 6-8 from 4 to 19 August. Floors 1-5 stayed at 8.5 (within normal variation). Floors 6-8 fell from 8.6 to 7.4, and room comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1. Their scores were 6.8 during the outage and recovered to 8.4 after the repair. 56 of the 74 negative comments were about heat, all from floors 6-8. Front-desk temperature complaints went from 1 to 24. Cleanliness scores (8.7 to 8.6) and inspection pass rates (95-96%) did not move after Orrin took over. Kiosk check-in scores and queue times were also stable. So I would not give notice to Orrin or pull the kiosks. The cooling failure followed a deferred maintenance decision. The 6% rate increase may have added a little to the value-score dip on floors 1-5. That dip is only slightly larger than the usual August seasonal one, so I can't separate the two. Don't reverse the rate yet. Next steps: restore the preventive maintenance on both chillers, keep critical spare parts on site, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. Report the August GSS unadjusted and annotate it. Don't exclude the floors 6-8 responses. Confidence is high, about 85-90%. I collected no further evidence.
